page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v5 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine belonging to the Dls_v5 series. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, complemented by Intel AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI.

The instance is provisioned with 96.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. This lower memory-to-core ratio prioritizes processing capacity over broad in-memory datasets. There is no bundled local ephemeral storage, meaning all persistence and operating file systems rely entirely on external Azure managed disks such as Premium SSDs. The instance features no discrete hardware GPUs, relying exclusively on CPU execution units.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing and cryptographic performance. The CPU architecture excels in multi-threaded tasks, scoring in the top 25 percent for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 221.23 GB/sec and PassMark CPU encryption at 43,318.73. High-throughput instruction processing also yields top-quartile results in image processing and CPU-based lightweight LLM inference on 135M and 7B parameter models. Conversely, general integer execution and system throughput in Geekbench multi-core, static web serving, and database transactions measure within average margins.

From an infrastructure perspective, the D48ls_v5 delivers cost efficiency for processing-heavy workloads that do not require standard 4 GB per vCPU general-purpose allocations. By reducing memory density to 2 GB per core, deployments avoid paying for surplus RAM. The primary operational tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, necessitating external storage configurations. This makes the instance suitable for distributed build agents, continuous integration pipelines, batch video and image transcoding, and moderate-footprint compute services.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v5 is a compute-focused x86_64 virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it supplies 96.0 GB of RAM alongside 48 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AVX-512 instructions. The instance incorporates no local disk storage, depending entirely on remote storage volumes, and does not include GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the D48ls_v5 registers upper-quartile results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, hardware-accelerated encryption, and CPU-based small-to-medium parameter LLM inference, while achieving mid-tier results in general database transactions and web serving. Because it avoids over-provisioning memory capacity, it provides an efficient compute architecture for CI/CD compilation, multi-threaded batch operations, cryptographic tasks, and CPU-driven media encoding pipelines.
